title: Opportunistic Burst Credits & SLA Tiering for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Run a paired pricing and contract experiment that introduces an 'opportunistic burst credits' construct for Dedicated capacity customers plus a clarified SLA tier matrix. Goal: reduce friction for sales when customers need short-term spikes without selling large committed GPUs, while preserving predictable economics and contract clarity for enterprise legal/compliance teams.
decisions: Adopt a two-part SKU: committed GPU lanes (monthly reservation) + opportunistic burst credits consumed independently
Burst credits priced as 1-week packs with explicit soft caps and a daily burst rate (tokens), instead of per-minute billing to reduce metering complexity

Define three SLA tiers (Standard, Business, Resilient) with p99 latency targets and differentiated burst guarantees — only Business+ receive guaranteed burst capacity during regional preemption events
Require a short security questionnaire addendum and KMS/Audit controls to enroll in Resilient SLA; treat Private/VPC customers as needing mandatory questionnaire review
tradeoffs: Complexity vs clarity: two-part SKU is slightly more complex for billing but easier for sales to explain than minute-granularity metering
Revenue predictability vs flexibility: burst credits reduce near-term committed revenue but increase conversion from proof-of-concept to paid Reserved customers
Operational risk: guaranteeing burst capacity in an oversubscribed pool requires stricter autoscale guardrails and preemption policies
Security gating: adding SQ gating may slow sales cycles for sensitive customers but reduces legal/infosec friction later
acceptance_criteria: Pricing model documented in Confluence with unit economics model showing impact across three customer personas
Pilot offer bundled and approved by Sales and Finance for 3 pilot accounts
Legal sign-off on contract language for burst credits, SLA definitions, and security questionnaire addendum
Telemetry spec created for billing events: committed-lane-hours, burst-credit-usage, burst-throttle-events
Console UX: new SKU toggle and burst credit meter visible in Console billing and quota pages for pilot customers
